BiblicalUsage: Kapnos is smoke — the sign of fire, whether the wonders in heaven above and signs in the earth beneath, blood and fire and vapour of smoke, or the smoke of the incense which came up with the prayers of the saints before God, or the smoke of torment ascending for ever and ever. Smoke rises from every fire, and the question is always which fire it comes from.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe smoke goes up from two altars: the incense of the prayers of the saints, and the torment of those who worshipped the beast. The same smoke that carries prayer to God carries judgment away from Him — and I want my prayers on the first altar.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
